newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway state-run phone company wants to be listed.
newsitem.headline: Norway state-run phone company wants to be listed.

text.p: The managing director of Norway's state-owned telecommunications company Telenor said in an interview published on Tuesday he wants the group to be partially privatised.
Tormod Hermansen was quoted by financial daily Dagens Naeringsliv as saying that he could see Telenor listed on the Oslo Bourse as well as on stock exchanges abroad.
He told the newspaper he would ask the government this year to raise investment capital for Telenor through share issues.

"We (Telenor) could imagine making two issues of between 2.5 and three billion crowns each. All in all, we would increase own capital by five to six billion crowns. We could see the share listed both internationally and in Oslo," he said.
He said he had no clear concept yet but said he saw both political and commercial reasons for listing Telenor.

Hermansen said a partial privatisation would make it easier for the minority Labour government to steer Telenor because shared ownership with private investors would put the company beyond the reach of parliament.
He said parliamentary controls could be detrimental to the commercial success of the company.

Telenor's monopoly on providing wireline voice services will be broken through legislation next year. The company is also facing increasing competition on the liberalised cellular phone market from private telecommunications firm NetCom GSM ASA.

"We have to be prepared to continue having a minority government after the elections (in September this year)," he said. "For Telenor, this poses a political risk that will be difficult to live with."

Hermansen, a member of the Labour Party, said he was unhappy that the opposition forced Telenor to increase its transfer of revenue to the state coffers in 1996 to 950 million crowns from the planned 550 million crowns.
He accused the opposition of seeking to choke state-owned companies like Telenor.
Telenor, which has 18,500 employees, had a turnover of 23 billion crowns last year, according to the Dagens Naeringsliv.
